common_name: Mucho Gusto Abelia (Compact Variegated Pink-Margined Abelia)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring in well-drained soil in full sun to light shade; compact, mounding habit suits foundation plantings and mixed borders.

directions: Mucho Gusto forms a dense, rounded mound of glossy green leaves edged in creamy white to soft pink, with new growth flushing a deeper rose-pink that intensifies in cool weather. Small, fragrant white-to-pale-pink trumpet flowers appear from late spring through fall on a compact frame that needs little pruning to keep its shape. It tolerates heat, humidity, and moderate drought once established, making it a low-maintenance choice for Gulf Coast foundation plantings and small-space borders.
sources: North Carolina State Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox

common_name: Pink Pinata Abelia (Bright Pink-Margined Variegated Abelia)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring in well-drained soil in full sun to light shade; foliage color intensifies with cooler fall temperatures.

directions: Pink Pinata carries green leaves broadly margined in bright pink that deepens through fall, giving the shrub a vividly colored, almost year-round display independent of its bloom. Clusters of small white, sweetly fragrant trumpet flowers open over a long season from late spring into autumn and draw butterflies and bees steadily. It handles heat and humidity well and needs only an occasional light shaping cut to maintain a full, rounded form in mixed borders.
sources: North Carolina State Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox

common_name: Poco Loco Abelia (Dwarf Chartreuse-to-Red Foliage Abelia)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring in well-drained soil in full sun to light shade; a true dwarf that rarely needs pruning to stay in bounds.

directions: Poco Loco stays under two feet tall, unusually compact for a flowering abelia, with new foliage emerging bright chartreuse-yellow before shifting to fiery orange-red tones in cooler weather, all against small white blooms scattered from summer into fall. Its dense, mounding habit fits tight foundation spaces, edging, and container plantings where full-size abelias would quickly outgrow the spot. It tolerates heat and humidity well and needs minimal pruning to maintain its naturally tidy shape.
sources: North Carolina State Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox

common_name: Ruby Anniversary Abelia (Deep Burgundy New-Growth Abelia)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring in well-drained soil in full sun to light shade; strongest ruby foliage color develops with full sun exposure.

directions: Ruby Anniversary produces new leaves in deep ruby-red that mature to glossy dark green, creating a two-toned effect across the plant as flushes of growth appear through the growing season. Small white, lightly fragrant trumpet flowers bloom over a long stretch from late spring into fall, attracting bees and butterflies. The shrub tolerates heat, humidity, and short dry spells well once established and holds a naturally rounded form with only light annual shaping.
sources: North Carolina State Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox

common_name: Tres Amigos Abelia (Three-Tone Copper-Gold-Green Foliage Abelia)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring in well-drained soil in full sun to light shade; foliage displays three colors simultaneously across a single plant.

directions: Tres Amigos earns its name from foliage that shows copper-orange new growth, golden-yellow mid-season leaves, and deep green mature leaves all present on the shrub at once, giving a constantly shifting multicolor display through the growing season. Small white, fragrant trumpet flowers appear from late spring into fall and draw pollinators steadily. It handles heat and humidity well and needs only light, infrequent pruning to maintain a full, rounded habit in mixed borders.
sources: North Carolina State Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox

common_name: Sweet Emotion Blaze Abelia (Bright Red-Orange New Growth Compact Abelia)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring in well-drained soil in full sun to light shade; distinct from the cold-hardy species-type Abelia mosanensis 'Sweet Emotion' already in the dataset, this is a compact Abelia x grandiflora hybrid selection.

directions: Sweet Emotion Blaze flushes new growth in fiery red-orange that gradually settles to green, giving a compact, mounding shrub repeated bursts of bright color through the growing season as it puts out new stems. Small white to blush-pink, sweetly fragrant trumpet flowers bloom from late spring through fall and are a reliable draw for bees and butterflies. It tolerates heat, humidity, and moderate drought once established, and its naturally tidy habit needs only occasional light shaping.
sources: North Carolina State Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring in well-drained soil in full sun to light shade; flower color is a deeper true pink than most white-flowered abelia selections.

directions: Pinky Bells stands out among abelias for flowers that stay a soft true pink rather than fading to white, opening in small bell-shaped clusters against glossy green foliage from late spring through fall. The compact, mounding habit fits foundation plantings and mixed borders without frequent pruning, and the persistent reddish calyces that remain after petals drop add extended color interest. It tolerates heat and humidity well and draws bees and butterflies reliably through its long bloom season.
sources: North Carolina State Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring in well-drained soil in full sun to light shade; distinct from the unrelated groundcover Sedum spurium 'John Creech' already in the dataset, this is a compact flowering Abelia hybrid shrub.

directions: John Creech Abelia carries small, glossy dark-green leaves on a dense, compact mound that stays notably lower and tighter than the species-type Abelia x grandiflora. Small white, lightly fragrant trumpet flowers open over a long season from late spring into fall, drawing bees and butterflies steadily. Its tidy, slow-growing habit suits foundation plantings and low hedges, and it tolerates heat and humidity well with only occasional light shaping.
sources: North Carolina State Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox

common_name: Plum Surprise Abelia (Purple-Flushed Variegated Dwarf Abelia)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring in well-drained soil in full sun to light shade; purple foliage tones deepen with cooler autumn temperatures.

directions: Plum Surprise combines creamy-white leaf margins with a plum-purple flush that intensifies through fall, giving this dwarf abelia a distinctive multicolor look beyond its small white summer-to-fall flowers. The compact, dense habit fits tight foundation spaces and mixed containers without requiring frequent pruning. It tolerates heat, humidity, and moderate drought once established, and draws bees and butterflies steadily through its long bloom period.
sources: North Carolina State Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox
